content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a comprehensive document in 2021 focusing on the development, attraction, recruitment, and retention of the health workforce in rural and remote areas. This publication aims to address the challenges of ensuring equitable access to healthcare services in underserved regions. 2. A study by Baguiya A, Portela A, Moyvisan A, Gerlach N, Gopal P, Sauvé C, and others is currently in preparation. It evaluates the effectiveness of male involvement interventions on maternal and newborn health outcomes, highlighting the potential impact of engaging men in improving health indicators. 3. Kunene B, Beksinska M, Zondi S, Mthembu N, Mullick S, Ottolenghi E, and colleagues conducted a study in South Africa, published in 2004 by the Population Council in Washington, D.C. This research explores the role of involving men in maternity care and its implications for maternal and newborn health. 4. The WHO released recommendations in 2018 on the use of home-based records for maternal, newborn, and child health. These guidelines emphasize the importance of accessible and accurate health records to improve health outcomes and continuity of care. 5. In 2019, the WHO published a guideline on digital interventions for strengthening health systems. This document provides evidence-based recommendations on leveraging digital technologies to enhance healthcare delivery and system efficiency. 6. The WHO also issued recommendations on maternal and newborn care to promote a positive postnatal experience. These guidelines aim to improve the quality of care provided to mothers and newborns during the postnatal period. 7. Annex 1 of the WHO guideline on maternal and newborn care includes a list of contributors to the guideline. The WHO Steering Group, based in Geneva, Switzerland, includes experts such as Rajiv Bahl, the Unit Head of the Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health and Ageing, and Tarun Dua, the Programme Manager of the Department of Mental Health and Substance Use, among others.
